text:
In June 2022 we spoke most as one on "the supreme court": sixty-one of us said it, peaking June 24. On that same day thirty-seven of us said "to overturn roe," a phrase first recorded from Mazie K. Hirono.

The other convergence was legislative. Forty-two of us said "safer communities act" and forty said "the bipartisan safer communities act," both peaking June 24; the bipartisan formulation was first recorded from Lindsey Graham. Thirty-four of us said "the boyfriend loophole," first recorded from Amy Klobuchar, and thirty-four said "background checks for."

Earlier in the month thirty-five of us said "our kids act" and thirty-three said "the protecting our kids act," first recorded from Robin L. Kelly, both peaking June 8.

Two peaks, then: the eighth around our kids act, the twenty-fourth around the court, roe, and the safer communities act. We converged where the record shows we converged.
